title.narrative: Fostering the socio-economic recovery of IDP- Women and Girls- in Cabo Delgado

description.narrative: Cabo Delgado Province has been plagued by an extensive and violent armed conflict since 2017, which has resulted in a continuous flow of internally displaced persons (IDP) that has so far reached more than 650,000 people, of whom women, young girls and children are the majority and constitute the more vulnerable group in need of special attention and assistance. According to the last DTM data as of January 2021, the displaced population is constituted by 32% of women and 45% of children. Due to the high number of displaced women, estimated at 215,000 of which 4,347 are pregnant women (according to DTM data), the (re) construction of housing may assert an added challenge to the process if the adopted approach does not have displaced women and girls at the center of the process. Possible housing solutions should be diversified according to the location and characteristics of the beneficiaries, being related to culture, way of life, availability of materials and, above all, financial capacity. In many cases during humanitarian crises and recovery processes it appears that housing and shelter models have in some ways not guaranteed minimum conditions of security and resilience, nor provided essential basic services and adequate land and property ownership to this vulnerable group.
